title: Civil Defence in Europe: An Initial Assessment
date_evidence: PDF chapter filenames on the IISS research paper page: 'Civil-Defence-in-Europe-An-Initial-Assessment_21042026_chapter-3.pdf' and parallel chapter PDFs; /research-paper/2026/04/ and /press/2026/04/ URL paths.
key_claim: Europe's civil defence is a patchwork: some governments have built durable whole-of-society systems while others remain chronically exposed, and resilience tends to be strengthened only in domains recently stress-tested; closing the gap requires not just more spending but a rethinking of how states, societies and the private sector prepare for threats that no longer respect the boundary between war and peace.
notes: Flagship IISS research paper from the Stockholm Civil Defence Forum; main institutional assessment anchoring the patchwork / whole-of-society framing. Date 21 April 2026 confirmed by PDF chapter filenames (e.g. '...21042026_chapter-3.pdf') and the /research-paper/2026/04/ and /press/2026/04/ paths. IISS HTML pages are JS-rendered, so audit_source_dates.py may return UNVERIFIABLE.

title: Commission invites 150 EU citizens to help shape future preparedness actions
date_evidence: Visible byline on DG ECHO news page: 'Publication date 19 March 2026'; URL slug ends '...2026-03-19_en'.
key_claim: One year after adopting the Preparedness Union Strategy, the Commission convened a European Citizens' Panel on Preparedness; the EU and member states are guiding the public toward 72-hour household self-sufficiency, integrating preparedness into school curricula, and convened an EU Preparedness Conference on 23-24 March 2026 bringing together public authorities, the private sector and civil society.
notes: Visible byline 'Publication date 19 March 2026'; DG ECHO author. Confirms the whole-of-society and household-preparedness strands.

title: Council adopts conclusions on advancing the EU's capacity to counter hybrid threats
date_evidence: Council press release byline 'Press release, 16 March 2026'; underlying document ST-7349-2026 headed 'Brussels, 16 March 2026'; URL contains '/2026/03/16/'.

title: Sabotage Threats Have Put Europe's Power Networks on Alert
date_evidence: <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-05-12T..."> on claimsjournal.com; URL path '/news/national/2026/05/12/337454.htm' encodes the publication date.
key_claim: Utilities and governments across Europe's eastern flank are hardening grids against sabotage, missile and drone threats; 30% of Europe's low-voltage distribution grids are more than 40 years old and past their planned operational life; the EU estimates about EUR 1.2 trillion of grid investment is needed by 2040; under EU defence-spending plans about EUR 250 billion is intended for areas such as cybersecurity and critical infrastructure (per Eurelectric); a January 2026 arson attack on power cables near Berlin left about 100,000 people without power for days.
verbatim_quote: 30% of Europe's low-voltage distribution grids are more than 40 years old
notes: Bloomberg article syndicated to Claims Journal (insurance trade press); authors Lars Paulsson, Maciej Martewicz, John Ainger. meta article:published_time 2026-05-12. Tier 3 quality-journalism corroboration for the threat environment and grid-hardening cost.

title: Resilience compliance as a board-level duty: mandatory counter-sabotage and business continuity measures
date_evidence: Gleiss Lutz article visible byline '30.01.2026'; references the KRITIS-Dachgesetz Bundestag vote of '29 January 2026' in the body.
key_claim: Germany's resilience-compliance package (KRITIS-Dachgesetz adopted by the Bundestag on 29 January 2026; NIS2 transposition act NIS2UmsuCG in force since 6 December 2025; updated Security Screening Act in force since 16 January 2026) imposes binding resilience, counter-sabotage and incident-reporting duties on companies well outside the traditional defence sector, including manufacturers and SMEs in critical supply chains; the cyber-resilience law will cover roughly 29,500 companies (up from about 4,500); administrative fines reach EUR 10 million or 2% of global turnover; management can be held personally liable; estimated annual NIS2 compliance costs reach EUR 2.3 billion.
notes: STRUCTURAL ANCHOR. Law-firm analysis (Tier 3) but the canonical detailed account of the German resilience-compliance legislative package, which is the most advanced national instantiation of the signal. Byline date 30.01.2026 (110 days before scan date, within the 3-6 month structural-anchor band).

title: Making critical entities more resilient (summary of Directive (EU) 2022/2557, the CER Directive)
date_evidence: EUR-Lex legislative summary page; no publication date displayed (evergreen reference). Underlying Directive (EU) 2022/2557 with Article 6 designation deadline 17 July 2026.
key_claim: The Critical Entities Resilience Directive ((EU) 2022/2557) requires EU member states to identify and designate critical entities by 17 July 2026 across eleven sectors; designated entities must carry out risk assessments, take technical, security and organisational resilience measures, and notify disruptive incidents; member states must adopt national resilience strategies.
notes: Evergreen EUR-Lex legislative summary, used for the CER Directive's legal framework and the 17 July 2026 critical-entity designation deadline (Article 6).
